h1: Face Massage in Uluwatu: Kobido, Gua Sha and Buccal Explained
title_tag: Face Massage in Uluwatu, Bali: Kobido, Gua Sha & Buccal
meta: The best face massages in Bali explained: Kobido for lifting, Gua Sha for de-puffing, Buccal for jawline. Durations, prices and where to book in Uluwatu.
intro: Bali is famous for its massages, but most of them focus on the body. A face massage works on the muscles, circulation and lymph of the face: it lifts, de-puffs and relaxes in a way a classic facial cannot. Here are the face massages worth trying in Bali, and how to choose.
body_html:
Face massage vs body massage

A body massage relaxes the whole body; a face massage targets the 40+ small muscles of the face, the jaw and the neck. Results are visible: a lifted look, less puffiness around the eyes and a more defined jawline, often right after one session.

The 4 face massages we offer

Massage Duration Price What it does Best for
Kobido (collagen cream) 30 / 60 min IDR 500K / 850K Japanese lifting technique, fast rhythmic movements, lymphatic drainage Natural lift, tired features
Gua Sha 30 min IDR 350K Stone tool with Centella oil, drains and relaxes Puffiness, tension, relaxation
Buccal 15 min IDR 250K Intra-oral massage of the jaw and cheek muscles Jawline definition, jaw tension
Relaxation Ritual 45 min IDR 550K Face, scalp and hands + LED + mask Pure relaxation, jet lag

All prices include 15% tax and service charge. All four are available in both Ungasan and Bingin.

Which one should you choose?

  • You want a visible lift before an event: Kobido 60 min, or Kobido + Buccal.
  • You wake up puffy after the flight or a night out: Gua Sha.
  • You clench your jaw or want a sharper jawline: Buccal, ideally 3 sessions.
  • You just want to switch off: Relaxation Ritual.

Combine it with a facial

A face massage works even better after a Korean Hydrafacial: skin is clean and hydrated, and the massage boosts circulation for extra glow. Our most popular pairing is the Ultimate Korean Glass Skin & Hydralift + Buccal Massage.

faq: What is the best face massage for lifting?
Kobido is the reference for a natural lifting effect. Buccal adds jawline definition.
It can feel intense on tight jaw muscles, but it should never be painful. Tell your therapist if you need lighter pressure.
How often should I get a face massage?
Once a week for a series of 3 to 5 for visible results, then monthly.
Can men book a face massage?
Yes. Buccal and Kobido are popular with men for jaw tension and a sharper profile.
